Jordan / Sam —

Thanks for the report and the graphs, Sam. I pulled traces and telemetry for BellBank's reserved pool (pool id rb-772) for the 08:00–09:30 window. Short summary of findings: 

1) Dedicated GPU pool utilization: sustained per-GPU token throughput near configured soft ceiling for ~25 minutes starting 08:28. Kernel-level queues show continuous enqueuing (batch buffer utilization > 92%).
2) KV cache pressure: customer workloads have a high prefix variance for the pricing route; salt churn is causing KV misses to spike, which increases per-token compute.
3) Routing behavior: requests exceeding the soft threshold are being routed to the fallback model variant (lower-cost variant) which explains the sudden change in latency/5xx profile.
4) Error breakdown: majority are transient 503s due to enqueue drops at the batcher when queue depth surpassed max_inflight. A smaller population (~8%) are 429s from rate-limiter backpressure.

Immediate mitigation options (ordered by speed to execute):
A) Emergency headroom burst: provision 8 extra GPUs into rb-772 from our dedicated reservoir for 4 hours (fastest; requires exec approval for overage).
B) Temporary routing tweak: lower the routing threshold to prefer on-demand fallback sooner but increase concurrency limits for BellBank to reduce enqueue drops (fast, low-risk, customer-visible).
C) Model-level knob: enable a conservative quantized variant for pricing route (saves ~18% token throughput) — requires model ops sign-off and QA run (30–90m).

Recommended path: combine B + C immediately (apply routing tweak + enable quantized variant) to reduce drops within 10–20m, and request A as a safety net if load does not stabilize.

I attached a pre-filled capacity-request-form.pdf for Marcus to process if we go with A; it includes estimated incremental cost for 8 GPUs for 4 hours.

Let me know if you want me on a bridge now — I'm starting the routing change now in the canary region and will roll to global if metrics improve.

- Rishi
